title: A. K. Erlang and the Birth of Traffic and Queueing Theory (1917)
explainer: Danish engineer A. K. Erlang worked out the mathematics of how many telephone lines an exchange needed to handle a given call volume without excessive waiting, publishing the foundational result in 1917; the standard unit of telephone and computing traffic load, the erlang, was named after him. The same queueing math he developed - how arrival rate, service time, and the number of servers trade off - is what underlies autoscaling rules, connection pools, and capacity planning for a cloud backend today.
